sentences.text: Prosaurolophus is a duck-billed dinosaur distinguished by a small, solid crest made of nasal bones that projects upward just in front of the eyes.
The largest known individual measured about 9 meters in total length, with a skull reaching 0.9 meters and a body mass of 3 metric tons.
Its skull featured a flat front widening into a beak for stripping leaves, while the back of the mouth held thousands of teeth for grinding vegetation.
A complete skeleton found in 1924 revealed a smooth ischium, proving that a previously assigned hocked bone belonged to a different genus.
Barnum Brown first recovered a skull from the Red Deer River in Alberta in 1915, leading to the formal description of the type species in 1916.
A second species, Prosaurolophus blackfeetensis, was later named by Jack Horner in 1992.
This large herbivore likely acted as a browser, feeding on conifer trees and bark from the ground up to a height of 4 meters.
Its sophisticated skull included continuously replaced dental batteries and soft tissue nasal sacs that may have aided in processing tough plants.
Researchers believe the solid bony crest and associated inflatable sacs served as methods for social display through visual and auditory signals.
Evidence from a Montana bonebed suggests these animals gathered near water sources during droughts and lived in groups for at least part of the year.
Comparisons of eye rings indicate Prosaurolophus may have been catemeral, active throughout the day with only short rest intervals.
The dinosaur belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae, a grouping first analyzed in detail by Weishampel and Horner in 1990.
John Ostrom identified a pseudonarial crest as a shared feature linking Prosaurolophus, Brachylophosaurus, and Saurolophus.
Prosaurolophus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 75.7 and 74.1 million years ago in the Campanian stage.

The exact placement of Prosaurolophus among hadrosaurines remains debated, with some studies questioning whether the differences between Prosaurolophus and Saurolophus are sufficient to support them as distinct species.
